transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12 15:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Jun (Redwood SE), Priya (BrightData Head of Search), Tom (BrightData ML Eng), Ana (BrightData SRE), Markus (Product)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
- Discovery focused on embeddings + reranking architecture for BrightData's product search.
- Key constraints: 5M vector scale, hybrid search with BM25 fallback, latency p95 targets ~70ms for k=10, throughput target 200 qps.
- Options: Redwood Hosted embeddings + vector DB, Redwood Dedicated serving with private VPC, or Private deployment for residency and KMS.
- Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmark config, dataset sample, POC kickoff.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Sofia from Redwood, and with me is Marcus and Jun on the SE side. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Priya: Hi, thanks. Busy week but good.
[00:09] Tom: Hello.
[00:11] Sofia: Cool. Quick call agenda - we want to understand your search stack, embedding dimensions, rerank flow and constraints so we can propose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options and a POC. Sound good?
[00:21] Priya: Yep, that's exactly right. I'll give context: BrightData is building a product search layer over 40M SKUs, but for the first POC we want to scope 5M vectors. Our current infra uses Elastic for text search and a small homegrown ANN for vectors, but it's flaky on volume. We're evaluating vector DBs and whether to push embeddings generation to the platform or do it ourselves.
[00:42] Marcus: Got it. When you say "homegrown ANN", any specific implementation, and what's the current vector dim?
[00:48] Tom: It's an HNSW variant, tuned in-house. We're using 1536-dim embeddings from a sentence-transformer model right now.
[00:55] Jun: 1536 is common, fine. Wanted to confirm: are you doing hybrid search today (BM25 + vector), or sequential rerank?
[01:03] Priya: Hybrid, yeah. We do a BM25 candidate generation with filters by category, then ANN over those candidates, then a lightweight cross-encoder rerank for top 10. But the reranker is slow when we have bursts, and the ANN retrieval recall drops at scale.
[01:16] Marcus: Understood. So the typical pattern we'd recommend: store dense vectors in an ANN-optimized store, use metadata filters for pre-filtering, run an approximate nearest neighbor retrieval to get N candidates, and then optionally run a cross-encoder on those N to produce final ordering. That cross-encoder is the expensive op so you want to minimize how many items you send it.
[01:33] Tom: Exactly. Our performance goal is p95 under 70ms for k=10 when serving 200 qps sustained. Is that realistic?
[01:41] Marcus: Depends on where things live. If you run the cross-encoder in the same Dedicated environment as your ANN and embeddings (no network egress), and use batching + async rerank, we can often hit those numbers. Hosted will be trickier because cross-encoder forwarding to a separate service and egress can add tens of ms.
[01:57] Priya: What about dimensionality tradeoffs? We were thinking of trying 1536 vs 768 to cut storage/costs.
[02:03] Jun: Dropping dims helps linear storage and ANN index size roughly proportionally; retrieval latency also usually improves. But recall can suffer depending on your dataset. Our suggestion: run a 2-step POC — compare 1536 vs 768 on a 1M subset for recall@10 and latency. That's what Marcus will send in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[02:20] Tom: For ANN backend, we're evaluating Pinecone and Milvus. Any Redwood recommendations?
[02:24] Marcus: Redwood integrates well with many vector stores; two patterns: 1) Redwood generates/store embeddings in your vector DB via API (we can push embeddings to Milvus/Pinecone), or 2) Redwood hosts embeddings and you query via Redwood’s API which proxies into your vector DB. For high throughput and lower latency, Dedicated co-located with your ANN is best. If you want managed simplicity, Hosted + Pinecone is fine for smaller scale but watch egress/cost.
[02:44] Markus: If we go Dedicated, what's the minimum commit and what's included?
[02:48] Sofia: We have a Dedicated offering with reserved GPU pools; typical commitments start at monthly plans sized for your target qps. We'll send pricing scenarios — dev, pilot, production — for different commit levels. Dedicated includes private networking and can be placed in your VPC for Private-like isolation if needed.
[03:05] Ana: We have strict residency and KMS requirements for EU data. Private deployment might be preferred. How mature is Redwood Private?
[03:11] Jun: We've done multiple Private installs with customer-managed KMS and audit logs. For GDPR, we support VPC deployments and can integrate with your KMS/HSM. The tradeoff is upfront integration work and slower rollout vs Hosted. We'll share the security pack.
[03:27] Priya: About rerank models — can Redwood host the cross-encoder or do we need to run it ourselves?
[03:32] Marcus: Redwood can serve rerank models as part of the serving runtime. You can bring your model (e.g., fine-tuned cross-encoder) or use one we host. Hosting reduces orchestration and helps keep latency tight if colocated. It's a compute tradeoff — cross-encoders are CPU/GPU heavy for per-request scoring.
[03:49] Tom: Do you support approximate candidate generation with IVF/ HNSW or other index types? And can we tune recall/latency knobs?
[03:55] Jun: Yes — we expose index-level params and recommend tuning ef/search_k for HNSW or probes for IVF during the POC. We can also simulate performance with our benchmarking harness. Marcus: We'll provide recommended knobs in the benchmark config.
[04:10] Priya: Filtering — we need strict category filters and geo-filters to be applied before ANN search. Does Redwood handle metadata filtering?
[04:16] Marcus: Yes, we support filtering at query time; best practice is to apply boolean metadata filters in the vector DB (or via route-level filters) so the ANN only scans the relevant shard. That reduces false positives and speeds rerank.
[04:27] Priya: About cost — for 5M vectors at 1536 dims with a monthly sustained 200 qps, do you have a ballpark on storage + serving cost?
[04:35] Sofia: We'll produce a Dedicated vs Hosted cost comparison. Roughly, storage scales with dims and replicas; inference cost depends on the rerank model and token generation if you also do generation. We'll include an apples-to-apples estimate in the SOW.
[04:47] Tom: One concern: our current ML pipeline runs embeddings offline at ingest, not on-demand. Does Redwood require you to compute embeddings through Redwood, or can we supply precomputed vectors?
[04:55] Jun: You can supply precomputed vectors. Option A — you compute embeddings at ingest (your preferred), push them into your vector DB and Redwood will talk to that DB for retrieval/rerank. Option B — Redwood host computes embeddings via our embeddings endpoint and writes to your DB. Both patterns are supported.
[05:13] Priya: For PII considerations, we'd prefer embeddings to be computed in our VPC or not leave EU. That's a point for Private or Dedicated.
[05:21] Marcus: Agreed. That's where Private shines. For Hosted we can consider region constraints and dedicated tenancy, but full KMS control is with Private or dedicated VPC setups.
[05:30] Tom: Let's talk throughput testing. What's a realistic POC bench plan?
[05:33] Marcus: Typical bench: ingest sample (1M) vectors, index config for HNSW with tuned efConstruction, run read QPS sweeps 50-200-500 for k=10, measure recall@10 and latency percentiles. Also test cross-encoder rerank latencies with batching for top N candidates (N=50, 100). We'll include a script for loadgen.
[05:53] Priya: Any gotchas migrating from Elastic+homegrown ANN to a hybrid system?
[05:57] Jun: Two things — (1) topology: ensure your ANN and rerank are colocated to avoid network hops; (2) ranking parity: cross-encoder behavior can re-order results relative to BM25, so you need labeled eval sets to measure quality. We'll help design eval prompts.
[06:13] Markus: We use multiple languages. Embedding models - any language coverage concerns?
[06:17] Marcus: Many embeddings models are multilingual, but you should pick and validate one that matches your languages. We'll help run a quick quality eval on your sample.
[06:25] Priya: Security checklist — SSO, RBAC, audit logs, data retention windows — do you provide logs we can ship to our SIEM?
[06:31] Jun: Yes. Audit logs, request traces and token-level cost logs are available. For Private we can stream logs into your SIEM. For Hosted we provide exports and integrations.
[06:41] Tom: For the POC acceptance criteria, what should we define?
[06:45] Marcus: Usually: ingest 1M vectors, achieve recall@10 > baseline (your current) and p95 latency < target (70ms) at 200 qps, plus a quality uplift measured by annotated set. We'll put that in the SOW.
[06:58] Priya: If we need deeper integration with Pinecone or Milvus, do you help with that in the POC?
[07:03] Sofia: Yes, SE support time is included for onboarding and index tuning in the POC. We'll outline SE days in the SOW.
[07:10] Tom: Any note about quantization or sparse embeddings to reduce space?
[07:14] Jun: Quantization is viable — int8 or product quantization reduces memory significantly with a small recall hit; it's a great lever to explore. We'll include a quantization run in the bench plan.
[07:25] Priya: Onboarding timeline — how fast can we get a pilot running?
[07:28] Marcus: Once we have the dataset slice and confirm the deployment mode, we can spin up a pilot in 1-2 weeks for Hosted; Dedicated/private will take longer due to provisioning and networking, 3-6 weeks typically.
[07:40] Markus: For the rerank cross-encoder, are you recommending GPU-backed inference?
[07:44] Jun: For latency targets at scale, yes GPUs are ideal. Dedicated GPU pools for inference give consistent p95s. CPU inference for small workloads is possible but less predictable.
[07:53] Ana: Our SRE wants to understand failover - if the re-ranker or vector DB gets slow, do you have graceful degradation?
[07:59] Marcus: We can route to a cheaper fallback model or return BM25-only results. Redwood has routing policies and automatic fallback to a lighter model variant if latency climbs. We'll show routing configs in the Console.
[08:12] Priya: How does caching fit in? Would caching candidate sets or rerank outputs help?
[08:16] Jun: Yes — prefix or KV caching for frequent queries reduces load; for shopping queries with heavy tail, caching top reranks can save a lot. Caching is something we'll tune during the POC.
[08:26] Tom: Will you be able to push logs of per-query cost so we can evaluate unit economics?
[08:30] Sofia: Absolutely, Redwood Console provides token-level and request-level cost breakdowns; we'll add an example for rerank cost per request in the SOW.
[08:40] Priya: Anything else we should be mindful of?
[08:42] Marcus: Make sure to provide representative metadata filters and at least one annotated eval set so we can measure quality. Also, tell us your expected growth curve; it affects index sharding and replica planning.
[08:55] Markus: We'll send expected QPS growth and data retention policy.
[08:58] Sofia: Great. Quick recap of next steps: Marcus sends benchmark spreadsheet + config; Sofia sends Dedicated pricing + SOW draft + security pack; Tom sends sample dataset slice and annotated eval set; schedule POC kickoff for week of 2025-02-24.
[09:16] Priya: That works.
[09:18] Tom: Sounds good.
[09:20] Sofia: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links.
[09:23] Priya: Thanks.
[09:25] End of meeting.
